mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary conditions, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month, it signals strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals accommodative monetary policy with potential inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek higher returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of low FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive but retail sales (RSAFS) are declining, it signals a divergence between macroeconomic growth and consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as market sentiment turns negative.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of positive GDPC1 growth and declining RSAFS on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
